topic: Octopus biology: hearts, blood, arms, taste, color
hook: 5 things octopuses do that seem impossible

slides.title: Three hearts
slides.body: Two hearts pump blood through the gills. The third pumps it to the rest of the body.
slides.image_prompt: An octopus floating in deep blue water with three glowing red hearts visible inside its translucent body, dramatic light rays from above

slides.title: Blue blood
slides.body: Their blood carries oxygen with copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron, which turns it blue.
slides.image_prompt: Glass vial of glowing blue liquid resting on wet rocks beside octopus tentacles, ocean background, cinematic lighting
slides.credit: Ahmed Abdul Rahman (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Arms that think
slides.body: About two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are in its arms, not its brain.
slides.image_prompt: Octopus arm curling around a seashell with faint glowing neural network lines running through it, dark ocean background

slides.title: They taste by touch
slides.body: Their suckers are packed with chemical receptors, so octopuses taste whatever they touch.
slides.image_prompt: Close-up of octopus suckers gripping a crab shell on the seafloor, soft underwater light, high detail

slides.title: Colorblind color masters
slides.body: They change color in a blink, yet most species have only one type of light receptor in their eyes.
slides.image_prompt: Octopus blending into colorful coral reef, half its body matching the coral pattern, vivid underwater scene
slides.credit: Jerome Paillet (IFREMER, Laboratoire d'Océanographie Physique et Spatiale, Centr (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

cta: Follow for facts you never knew
caption:
Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood and arms that can taste. They look less like animals from Earth and more like visitors from another planet.

One of the strangest details: about two-thirds of their neurons sit in their arms, so each arm can explore and react on its own.

Which of these octopus facts surprised you the most?
